data.title: A nutrient-induced affinity switch controls mTORC1 activation by its Rag GTPase-Ragulator lysosomal scaffold
data.authors: Lawrence RE; Cho KF; Rappold R; Thrun A; Tofaute M; Kim DJ; Moldavski O; Hurley JH; Zoncu R

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: A nutrient-induced affinity switch in the Rag-Ragulator scaffold controls mTORC1 lysosomal recruitment.
data.abstract_excerpt: A key step in nutrient sensing is activation of the master growth regulator, mTORC1 kinase, on the lysosomal membrane. Nutrients enable mTORC1 scaffolding by a complex composed of the Rag GTPases (Rags) and Ragulator, but the underlying mechanism of mTORC1 capture is poorly understood. Combining dynamic imaging in cells and reconstituted systems, we uncover an affinity switch that controls mTORC1 lifetime and activation at the lysosome.
